name: Mr. Boom
description: Mr. Boom is a Bomberman-style action game for up to eight players, originally made for MS-DOS by Remdy Software in the late 1990s. Its original author later converted the x86 assembly to C and released it as an open-source libretro core and SDL2 game. It adds AI bots, team modes and network play.
curiosities: The original DOS assembly code was converted to C with a tool called asm2c rather than rewritten by hand.
It supports up to eight players at once, more than most Bomberman games.
Players can ride kangaroos, push bombs and trigger them with remote controls.
Its team modes include grouping players by colour or pitting humans against bots.
story: Mr. Boom is a free Bomberman-style game started in 1997, playable by up to eight players.
It was made by fans and is now available on many systems through libretro.
It keeps the multiplayer spirit of Bomberman alive.
